text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Only 250 Finnish army concscripts volunteered to join rapid reaction force.

- Sweden's former prime minister Carl Bildt suggests pertnership for peace agreement between the Balitc countries and NATO. Bildt says this would create a stable defense policy environement in the Baltic and Nordic area.
- Petrol price competion is heating up in Helsinki -- the cheapest 95-octane petrol now costs 4.89 markka per litre.
KAUPPALEHTI

- Nokia suspected to be among reasons for huge lossess at investment bank Deutsche Morgan Grenfell's European investment funds -- 10 percent or 1.5 billion markka of the funds' investments were in Nokia.
- Merita bank has spent 30 million markka in restructuring bicycle manufacturer Tunturipyora.
- Asset management company Arsenal's clients' ability to pay interest has improved. Client liabilities decreased to 5.7 billion markka from 7.3 billion.
- Dividends from state-owned companies will not increase on companies' 1996 earnings -- the 1997 state budget expects the state to collect 1.2 billion markka in dividends.
DEMARI

- The Finnish Confederation of Salaried Employees says the special pay rise allotment for female workers in the incomes agreement should be paid out directly to women in order to smooth out growing pay differences betweeen the sexes.
- Pharmaceuticals sales have increased 10 percent year-on-year in Finland, study says.
- Social democrat Seppo Nevala appointed as chief of Security Police.
- Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen is travelling to the United States on Sunday to attend the Socialist International congress in New York.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- Swedish furniture retailer IKEA opens its doors today in Finland -- 30 years later after purchasing the property.
TURUN SANOMAT

- Many Finnish men have shown interest to pay 15,000 markka to increase the length of their pennis by plastic surgery, says Pirita health centre in Tallin, which advertised the service in some Finnish newspapers.
